note: Animated reconstruction driven by actual Python engine decisions; not a browser screen recording.

scenes.title: ParkWise
scenes.subtitle: EXPLAINABLE PARKING IN MOTION
scenes.caption: An animated demonstration of the working rule engine. All prices, sensors and vehicles are synthetic.

scenes.title: One facility. Ten bays.
scenes.subtitle: GROUND • UPPER DECK • CHARGING COURT
scenes.caption: Every bay has a type, size limit, hourly rate and operational status. The system searches for a suitable space.

scenes.title: A car arrives at 09:00
scenes.subtitle: R1 • CAR • 09:00–10:00 • BUDGET PKR 500
scenes.caption: R1 meets the account, time, size and budget conditions. G1 is the nearest eligible bay; G2 is an alternative.

scenes.title: Why was G1 selected?
scenes.subtitle: FORWARD CHAINING + INDEPENDENT BACKWARD PROOF
scenes.caption: Forward chaining derives the candidate from facts. Backward chaining independently verifies the same goal.

scenes.title: A second car requests the same time
scenes.subtitle: R2 • 09:00–10:00 • OVERLAPPING REQUEST
scenes.caption: G1 already has an overlapping booking. The engine excludes G1 and recommends G2 without double-booking.

scenes.title: An electric vehicle needs charging
scenes.subtitle: R3 • EV • CHARGING REQUIRED
scenes.caption: Only a compatible charging bay with a working charger can qualify. E1 passes; E2 has a charger fault.

scenes.title: Accessible parking is protected
scenes.subtitle: R4 • ACCESSIBILITY BADGE PRESENT
scenes.caption: The badge satisfies the accessible-bay rule. A1 is the nearest eligible option. Without a badge, it would be excluded.

scenes.title: A maintenance closure changes the plan
scenes.subtitle: G1 CLOSED • R1 STILL HAS ITS RESERVATION
scenes.caption: Closing G1 blocks new allocations. The existing R1 booking stays visible so the operator can handle the disruption.

scenes.title: A failed move must not lose the booking
scenes.subtitle: SAFE FAILURE • ORIGINAL RESERVATION RETAINED
scenes.caption: G2 is occupied and no other bay fits R1. Reallocation fails safely: R1 is not cancelled or silently discarded.
lines: Search without R1 only in copy

scenes.title: A cancellation releases G2
scenes.subtitle: R2 CANCELLED • CAPACITY BECOMES AVAILABLE
scenes.caption: The operator cancels R2. Its interval is released, allowing R1 to be evaluated for a replacement.

scenes.title: R1 moves safely to G2
scenes.subtitle: SUCCESS • REPLACE ONLY AFTER AN ELIGIBLE BAY IS FOUND
scenes.caption: The engine proves G2 eligible. Only then is R1 replaced in one state update. The animation shows the new assignment.

scenes.title: At 10:00, the next interval can begin
scenes.subtitle: HALF-OPEN INTERVALS • [START, END)
scenes.caption: A booking ending at 10:00 does not overlap one starting at 10:00. Completed intervals stop blocking later requests.

scenes.title: Unknown is not the same as free
scenes.subtitle: INDEPENDENT TEST CASE • SENSOR UNCERTAINTY
scenes.caption: An unknown reading on G1 produces a manual-review conclusion. The system recommends G2 instead of assuming G1 is empty.

scenes.title: A compact car finds a cheaper option
scenes.subtitle: INDEPENDENT TEST CASE • HEIGHT 1.6 M • BUDGET PKR 60
scenes.caption: G3 fits the smaller vehicle and costs PKR 50. More expensive or incompatible spaces are excluded before ranking.

scenes.title: Every decision has a reason.
scenes.subtitle: PARKWISE • KNOWLEDGE REPRESENTATION & REASONING
scenes.caption: Frames, semantic relationships, formal logic and Horn rules work together to explain parking decisions.
